title: harness: TokenLimiter in outputProcessors hung every tool call (FIXED — was mislabeled upstream)
description: In Agent Harness mode, certain prompts deterministically stall the session. agent_start fires and the user message echoes, but the model generation step never starts: display_state stays generationCount:0 with pendingApproval:null, activeTools:{}, toolInputBuffers:{}, pendingSuspensions:{}. No tool_call, no browser launch (no chromium in logs), no error, no log activity — the SSE just emits display_state heartbeats until the client gives up. Repro (live OpenAI, CHAT_MODEL=openai/gpt-4.1-mini): POST /harness/stream {text:'Look up the current top headline on Hacker News (news.ycombinator.com). Browse there and tell me the #1 story title right now.'}. Reproduces with webSearch ON and OFF (D1) — so it is NOT the web-search toggle (cco). Trivial ('reply hello') and substantive non-browse prompts ('explain a hash map in two sentences') complete cleanly. Suspects to investigate: workspace tool-calling loop with gpt-4.1-mini when the prompt implies browsing/URLs; the model router path for openai/*; defaultInputProcessors reacting to URLs; or the OpenAI tool-call stream never finalizing. Found while verifying cco.
design: ROOT CAUSE (isolated 2026-07-25, live OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini, cold-booted server): the AgentController/harness path (session.sendMessage) hangs at generationCount:0 on ANY turn where the model emits a tool call. Pure-text turns complete normally. The SAME chatAgent + SAME tools + SAME model works perfectly via the AI-SDK single-agent route (POST /chat/chat -> handleChatStream): 'weather in Paris, use getWeather' returned tool-input-delta stream + tool-output {temperatureC,condition} + finish in 3s. Via the harness it hangs. So the bug is in @mastra/core AgentController's handling of streamed OpenAI tool calls, NOT our code. Bisection that led here: (1) reproduces with webSearch ON and OFF -> not the web-search toggle (cco); (2) reproduces with the workspace browser DISABLED (createChatHarness({browser:null})) -> not the browser or its browser-context input processor; (3) 'forbid tools, answer from memory' completes in 2s, 'force the innocuous demo searchKnowledge tool' hangs -> it is the tool CALL, not the prompt topic; (4) during the hang: NO chromium spawns, NO tool_call/approval event, pendingApproval:null, activeTools:{}, toolInputBuffers:{} -> the generation never surfaces the tool call (hang is upstream of the HITL gate, not the gate waiting for approval).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified; browse-style prompts either produce a generation (answer or a gated browser tool call) or a clear error within a few seconds — never a silent generationCount:0 stall. Repro above returns a non-empty result or an approval gate.
notes: ALPHA TEST (2026-07-25, user-greenlit): pinned @mastra/core=1.53.0-alpha.2 via pnpm.overrides (the 'alpha' dist-tag, newest; supersedes 1.52.2-alpha.0). Server typechecked clean, non-tool chat worked, but the getWeather harness tool call STILL hangs identically (generationCount:0, no agent_end) on a guaranteed-fresh rebuild. So NO published @mastra/core version (stable 1.52.1 or any alpha) fixes the AgentController OpenAI tool-streaming hang. Reverted to 1.52.1 (clean). REMAINING FIX PATHS: (a) file an upstream mastra issue with the AI-SDK-works-vs-AgentController-hangs repro; (b) test disabling AgentController tool-approval gating (auto-approve) — the hang is at generationCount:0 before any approval event, so it MIGHT be the gating machinery deadlocking with OpenAI tool streaming; worth a direct test.
close_reason: FIXED in commit d290068 — and it was OUR config, not upstream (I misdiagnosed it earlier; the user pushed to search/re-check, which was correct). ROOT CAUSE: TokenLimiter/CostGuard implement only processInputStep; sitting in this kit's defaultOutputProcessors (@mastra/core >=1.47) they have no valid hook and break the response — on the AgentController streaming path they HANG the run mid tool-call (generationCount:0). Pure-text turns survived, which made it look OpenAI/provider-specific. ISOLATION: a minimal AgentController repro (bare agent + OpenAI + one tool) GATES and completes fine; adding the default processors reproduced the hang mid tool-input; removing TokenLimiter from the output slot fixed the exact production config. VERIFIED end-to-end on the live /harness/stream route: tool streams -> tool_approval_required -> approve -> tool_end (result) -> answer -> agent_end. SIDE FINDINGS: (1) the AgentController gates tool calls by default; the web UI's Confirmation element must approve them (already wired). (2) memory.ts generateTitle still hardcodes an Anthropic model — harmless now but should follow env.CHAT_MODEL for OpenAI-only setups (filed separately if needed). Matches vault note reference_mastra_tokenlimiter_output_bug; other mastra-* templates that copied the processor baseline need the same fix.

title: harness: fix OpenAI/non-Anthropic support — wire env.CHAT_MODEL + normalize null message content
description:
The Agent Harness engine never worked with non-Anthropic providers. Two root causes, both fixed this session (uncommitted):
(a) harness.ts hardcoded the AgentController mode model ('anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6') instead of reading env.CHAT_MODEL — so the harness ignored CHAT_MODEL (chatAgent.ts already honored it, but the AgentController mode defaultModelId overrode it). Fixed: CHAT_MODEL_ID = env.CHAT_MODEL.
(b) packages/web/lib/harness/events.ts crashed with 'm.content is not iterable' — OpenAI emits assistant messages with content:null (pure tool-call turns / message shells). The reducer trusted event.message as-is; every consumer (collectToolResults, renderContent) assumed an array. Fixed: normalizeContent() coerces null/string content to an array at upsertMessage.
RECONCILIATION: issue ykz (closed 2026-06-23) claimed 'made chatAgent read env.CHAT_MODEL' + 'real OpenAI smoke on BOTH engines' — but the current AgentController harness re-hardcoded the model AND the web harness UI (built later) was never exercised with OpenAI, so its content:null path crashed. ykz's Single-Agent half holds (chat.ts:145); this issue covers the harness half that regressed / was never truly covered.

title: web: Shiki CodeBlock SSR hydration mismatch on /showcase
description: The vendored CodeBlock (Shiki dual light/dark theme) emits inline color styles at SSR that differ from the client render, causing a React hydration mismatch warning when a CodeBlock is server-rendered (visible on /showcase via Tool input + Code Block cards). Cosmetic — React regenerates the subtree on the client and the page works. Proper fix lives in the vendored code-block.tsx (e.g. render code blocks client-only or suppressHydrationWarning on the pre/code). Same class of documented compromise as ignoreBuildErrors.
close_reason: Fixed Shiki CodeBlock SSR hydration mismatch. Root cause: highlightCode() reads a module-level tokensCache that lives for the whole Node process, so once the server highlights a block, later SSR renders emit COLORED tokens while every fresh client's first (hydration) render emits plain rawTokens (cold cache) -> React hydration mismatch (intermittent, depends on server cache warmth). Fix in code-block.tsx CodeBlockContent: added a mounted gate (useState(false)+useEffect setMounted(true)); tokenized = mounted ? (asyncTokens ?? syncTokens) : rawTokens. Forces SSR + client first render to both be rawTokens regardless of cache, then applies Shiki after mount. Verified live (agent-browser + curl): after warming server cache with 3+ SSR fetches, SSR HTML emits 0 server-side hex token colors (only color:inherit/transparent), console shows no hydration warnings, no page errors, and tokens highlight post-mount (real rgb color). typecheck 0, 63/63 vitest.

(2) The session-centric API FLIP landed in 1.46.0: the controller's direct-drive methods (subscribe/sendMessage/createThread/switchThread + .session getter) were REMOVED and replaced by createSession() -> Session. Session has always required a Workspace, so 1.46.0 is effectively where 'you now need a workspace' became true. (3) The class/file RENAME Harness -> AgentController (@mastra/core/harness -> @mastra/core/agent-controller; harness.d.ts -> agent-controller.d.ts) landed in 1.47.0; 'Harness' remains a deprecated alias. New driving flow: controller.createSession({resourceId,threadId?}) or getSessionByResource() -> Session with session.subscribe(listener), session.sendMessage({content}), session.abort(), session.respondToToolApproval({decision}), session.thread.create/switch/requireId(). Workspace must be configured on the AgentController (workspace: new Workspace({id, filesystem: new LocalFilesystem({basePath})})) OR passed per createSession; empty Workspace throws 'requires at least a filesystem, sandbox, or skills'. allowedWorkspaceTools is a SUBAGENT field, not a mode field. core 1.52 bundles @ai-sdk/provider-v5/v6/v7 so it supports AI SDK v7.

Migrating a Mastra template from Postgres (@mastra/pg) to libSQL/Turso (@mastra/libsql) — gotchas found in mastra-chat-kit: (1) STORE SWAP is clean: PostgresStore->LibSQLStore (url: file: local / libsql:// prod, needs id), PgVector->LibSQLVector (option is 'url' NOT 'connectionUrl', + id + authToken). LibSQL has native vector search so no pgvector/DuckDB. (2) RELATIVE file: PATHS SPLIT under : the server cwd differs between module load and request time, so file:./mastra.db resolves to TWO files (agent writes threads to src/mastra/public/, other ops elsewhere) -> empty reads. Fix: absolutize file: URLs (resolve at load) AND/OR pass an absolute TURSO_DATABASE_URL. (3) BATCHED ARRAY BIND breaks on libSQL: memory.recall({threadId: idsArray}) (or any getThreadById with an array) throws 'SQLite3 can only bind numbers, strings, bigints, buffers, and null' and 500s the route — Postgres silently tolerated the array. Recall per-thread with a single string id. (4) e2e: mastra dev honors PORT env (no --port flag); killing by port doesn't reliably kill mastra dev's process tree (zombies hold a per-project lock -> 'Another development server instance is already running') — kill by command-line match.
